Subject: Sustained backlog on reserved pool — API 5xx and tail latency

Jasmine,

We started seeing a gradual but steady buildup in queued requests to our reserved pool at ~03:15 UTC and it hasn't cleared. Our production error rate (5xx) has climbed to ~2.7% and p99 latency jumped from 180ms to ~1.8s for text-generation calls. This is hitting our checkout flows (orders stalled).

Attached are a short error sample and a screenshot from our telemetry showing queue depth over the last 3 hours. Can you confirm whether this is local to our instance or a wider pool saturation? We signed up for committed capacity specifically to avoid this.

We need: 1) immediate triage and mitigation plan, 2) estimated time to recovery, and 3) path to prevent recurrence (we're evaluating retention of Dedicated). Also expect this will require exec visibility from our side — they'll want credits if this becomes a repeat.

Thanks,
Samir Patel

BlueForge Capital

Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sustained backlog on reserved pool — API 5xx and tail latency

Team — quick snapshot from infra: we're seeing sustained queue depth on the customer's dedicated pool nodes (pool-id: ded-us-west-7). Two processes are showing elevated KV cache eviction and one node is reporting intermittent OOM-restarts in the last hour. This aligns with increased tail latency and retries generating a feedback loop.

Immediate mitigation plan (actioned):
- Evacuate non-critical canary traffic off ded-us-west-7 (in progress)
- Temporarily widen autoscale trigger to allow burst allocation + enable immediate short-lived burst capacity from spare host pool (30 min window)
- Increase per-request concurrency limit for the customer's routes to reduce queueing pressure (will slightly increase per-token cost but reduce queues)

ETA: stabilization expected within 18-30 minutes after burst capacity provisioned; full p99 recovery within 60-90 minutes pending no further noisy neighbors.

We should also prepare: a post-incident runbook note (root cause: uneven KV cache pressure + one noisy tenant causing memory compaction) and an ops request for a small additional reservation or sustained headroom.

I'll stand by on the bridge and we should update Samir now.

-David
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sustained backlog on reserved pool — API 5xx and tail latency

Update for Jasmine / Samir — we executed the mitigation plan: burst capacity was allocated at 09:12 UTC, canary traffic removed, and per-route concurrency widened. Observed results: p50 ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 220ms, p99 drifted down to ~260-320ms and 5xx has fallen to 0.4% over the last 20 minutes. Queue depth has decreased to baseline.

Next steps we propose to share with BlueForge today: 
1) Short-term: keep burst capacity active for 2 hours while we monitor for reoccurrence. If no further pressure, we'll scale the burst down in controlled increments.
2) Medium-term (ops recommendation): add +15% guaranteed headroom to their dedicated reservation or schedule a predictable daytime burst window. I'll prepare an ops change request with capacity numbers.
3) Commercial: given the customer impact during their window, recommend offering a one-time service credit (we should discuss amount) and commit to a joint postmortem.

Jasmine — want to sync with you on the credit wording and whether Sales should pre-authorize a credit up to $Xk. Vivek / Grace — can you join a 30-min exec bridge at 16:00 PST for BlueForge execs? Samir, Priya — we propose a short remediation note and a 1:1 postmortem tomorrow with their engineering leads.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
